text: When the day of Pentecost finally arrived, all the believers were gathered together in a single place.
Out of nowhere came a noise from the sky like a violent gust of wind, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting.
Something resembling flames split apart and came to rest on each person there.
Every one of them was filled with the Holy Spirit and started speaking in languages they had never learned, as the Spirit gave them the words.
Jerusalem at that time was packed with devout Jews who had come from every nation under the sky.
When the noise was heard, a crowd gathered, and they were confused because each person heard the believers speaking in his own native language.
They were stunned and asked one another, 'Aren't all these people speaking Galileans?'
'Then how is each of us hearing our own mother tongue?'
'Parthians, Medes, and Elamites; people from Mesopotamia, Judea, Cappadocia, Pontus, and the province of Asia;'
'from Phrygia and Pamphylia, Egypt, and the parts of Libya near Cyrene; visitors from Rome;'
'both born Jews and converts to Judaism, along with Cretans and Arabs — we all hear them talking about God's mighty deeds in our own languages.'
Amazed and thoroughly confused, they kept asking each other what this could possibly mean.
But others just laughed it off, saying the whole crowd had simply had too much wine.
Then Peter stood up with the other eleven, raised his voice, and addressed the crowd directly: 'Fellow Jews, and everyone staying here in Jerusalem, listen carefully and let me explain.'
'These people are not drunk, as you assume — it's only nine o'clock in the morning.'
'What you're seeing is exactly what the prophet Joel spoke about.'
'God says: in the last days I will pour out my Spirit on everyone — your sons and daughters will speak my message, your young men will see visions, your old men will dream dreams.'
'Even on my male and female servants I will pour out my Spirit in those days, and they will speak for me.'
'I will display wonders above in the sky and signs below on the earth — blood, fire, and thick smoke.'
'The sun will go dark and the moon will turn blood-red before the great and dramatic day of the Lord comes.'
'And everyone who calls on the Lord's name will be rescued.'
'People of Israel, hear this: Jesus of Nazareth was a man clearly marked out by God, shown to you through miracles, wonders, and signs God performed through him, as you well know.'
'He was handed over according to God's own settled plan and foreknowledge, and you had him killed, nailing him up by the hands of lawless men.'
'But God raised him back to life, releasing him from death's grip, because death had no way to hold on to him.'
'David said about him: I kept the Lord in front of me always; because he stands at my right hand, nothing can shake me.'
'That's why my heart is glad and my words are full of joy; even my body will rest secure in hope.'
'You will not leave me among the dead, nor let your holy one rot away.'
'You have shown me the road to life; your presence will fill me with joy.'
'Friends, I can tell you plainly that our ancestor David died and was buried, and his tomb is still here among us today.'
'But he was a prophet, and he knew God had sworn to him that one of his own descendants would sit on his throne.'
'Seeing this ahead of time, he spoke about the Christ's resurrection — that he would not be left among the dead, nor would his body rot away.'
'This Jesus is the one God raised to life, and every one of us here can testify to it.'
'Lifted up to God's right hand, he received the promised Holy Spirit from the Father and has now poured out what you are seeing and hearing.'
'David himself never went up to heaven, yet he is the one who said, the Lord told my Lord, sit here at my right hand,'
'until I make your enemies a footstool under your feet.'
'So let all of Israel know for certain: God has made this very Jesus, whom you crucified, both Lord and Messiah.'
'Hearing this pierced them to the core, and they asked Peter and the rest of the apostles, brothers, what should we do?'
'Peter told them: turn back to God and be baptized, every one of you, in Jesus Christ's name so your sins can be forgiven, and you will be given the Holy Spirit.'
'This promise belongs to you, to your children, and to everyone far away — everyone the Lord our God calls to himself.'
'He kept warning and pleading with them at length, urging them to save themselves from this twisted generation.'
'Those who believed what he said were baptized, and about three thousand people joined the group that day.'
'They devoted themselves steadily to the apostles' teaching, to fellowship together, to sharing meals, and to prayer.'
'A sense of awe came over everyone, and the apostles performed many wonders and signs.'
'All the believers stayed together and shared everything they owned.'
'They sold land and belongings and distributed the money to anyone who was in need.'
'Day after day they met together in the temple courts, and they shared meals in each other's homes with joyful, generous hearts,'
'praising God the whole time and earning the goodwill of everyone around them. And every day the Lord kept adding to their number those who were being saved.'
